articles.title: Free agents: Jadon Sancho, Paul Pogba and Dele Alli among players available on free transfer after summer window shuts
articles.summary: Free agents available after summer transfer window shuts; host of stars including Jadon Sancho, Paul Pogba and Dele Alli looking for new clubs: Sky Sports presents a free agent squad packed with World Cup winners, Champions League veterans and domestic league champions
articles.body:
Jadon Sancho , Paul Pogba and Dele Alli are among some of the big names on the free agency market, so could your club give them the opportunity to rediscover their once world-class level?

Here, Sky Sports presents a free agent squad packed with World Cup winners, Champions League veterans and domestic league champions…

Values below reflect players' historic peak market value according to transfermarkt.

After his year-long loan with Arsenal from Bournemouth ended in 2025, Neto joined Botafogo but decided to terminate his contract by mutual consent in June. His disappointing stint in Brazil was summed up in his final game for the club, receiving a red card for time-wasting and swearing at the referee.

Right-back: Dani Carvajal, 34 - £51.5m in 2018

Arguably one of the best right-backs of his generation, Carvajal left Real Madrid after 23 years this summer. During his time at the Spanish giants, he made 450 appearances, and leaves as one of the most decorated players in history with 27 titles, including six Champions League titles.

Centre-back: Sergio Ramos, 40 - £43m in 2018

Another Real Madrid icon finds himself on the free agent list. Ramos joined Los Blancos in 2005 and spent 16 years at the club, scoring 101 goals in 671 appearances, winning 23 trophies along the way. He's since played for PSG, Sevilla and most recently Mexican side Monterrey, and despite not having had a club since January 2026, the Spanish icon is yet to announce his retirement from football.

Centre-back: David Alaba, 34 - £55.8m in 2018

Former Bayern Munich and Real Madrid defender Alaba is on the free agent market after Real decided not to renew the 34-year-old's contract this summer. An illustrious career consisting of 35 trophies, including 12 league titles and four Champions Leagues, the Austrian could be an asset to any club looking to bolster their defensive unit.

Left-back: Oleksandr Zinchenko, 29 - £36m in 2023

Four-time Premier League winner Zinchenko is without a club since his injury-ridden spell at Ajax reduced the Ukrainian to just 20 minutes on the pitch. He was previously on loan at Nottingham Forest from Arsenal for the 2025/26 season, but Forest decided to cut it short in January after limited game time.

Central midfielder: Paul Pogba, 33 - £85.9m in 2019

The 2018 World Cup-winning midfielder signed for Ligue 1 side Monaco on a two-year deal last summer after serving an 18-month football suspension for a doping offence. However, the contract was terminated this summer by mutual consent.

Central midfielder: Dele Alli, 30 - £85.9m in 2018

The once wonderkid - who produced an 18-goal 2016/17 Premier League campaign for Spurs and helped England reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals - has struggled in recent years with injuries and form. Alli has been without a club since his contract was terminated at Como in 2025 by mutual consent but has yet to officially retire.

Central midfielder: Philippe Coutinho, 34 - £128.8m in 2018

Former Liverpool and Barcelona midfielder Coutinho has been a free agent since he left his boyhood club Vasco da Gama in February. The Brazilian struggled to reach the levels he showed at Liverpool since signing for Barcelona in a mega-money move in 2018.

Right-wing: Raheem Sterling, 31 - £137.4m in 2019

Having been released by Feyenoord after just three months, Sterling has been through a difficult period on-and-off the pitch. Last month he was charged with dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide and is due to appear at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court for a hearing on September 15. Football-wise, he hasn't scored since September 2024, when he bagged Arsenal's fourth in a 5-1 victory over Bolton in the Carabao Cup.

Left-wing: Jadon Sancho, 26 - £111.6m in 2020

It's been five years since Sancho's £73m move to Man Utd from Borussia Dortmund, and according to Sky in Germany , talks have taken place with his former club after indicating a willingness to join. The winger most recently featured in Aston Villa's Europa League-winning squad.

Striker: Karim Benzema, 38 - £51.5m in 2016

The 2022 Ballon d'Or winner has spent the last three years in Saudi Arabia, spending two-and-a-half years with Al Ittihad before moving to Al Hilal on a one-and-a-half-year deal, which was terminated by mutual agreement this summer.

Riyad Mahrez (£51.5m), Georginio Wijnaldum (£43m), Wilfried Zaha (£47.2m), James Rodriguez (£68.7m), Yves Bissouma (£30m), Tyrell Malacia (£18.9m), Jamie Vardy (£17.2m), Anthony Martial (£55.8m), Chris Smalling (£17.2m).

articles.title: How Deion Sanders and Colorado overcame sloppy play to eke out crucial win over Georgia Tech — 'Just damn violence'
articles.summary: It certainly wasn't pretty, but the Buffaloes are 1-0 and Coach Prime's team actually impressed in some ways in its opener.
articles.body:
ATLANTA — After he had left the field arm-in-arm with his son Shedeur, after the Colorado players spilled from the sideline to their families in the corner of Bobby Dodd Stadium to celebrate a truly remarkable season-opening win over Georgia Tech, and after athletic director Fernando Lovo hugged and chest-bumped Buffaloes great Kordell Stewart as they headed toward the locker room, Deion Sanders sat down at a table wearing gray stubble, no sunglasses and a black trucker-style hat.

Knowing what we know about Coach Prime, and having watched what we just watched — Colorado blocking a 45-yard field goal to win 14-13 — it felt like a moment for sermons and told-you-sos.

But 17 minutes later, in perhaps the biggest upset of the night, there was none of that.

For the first time since he became a college head coach, Prime's team came into a season under the radar.

It exits its opening game with something more valuable than hyperbole: A win that, perhaps for the first time in his coaching career, was about the product on the field, and not the circus he constructed around it.

"This is a big win for these kids, man," Sanders said. "I'm straight, man. I don't, I don't shake a shadow. We know what we doing here. We don't shatter. We let y'all talk. You got to sell some papers. You got to get some clicks. You got to do that. So talk your talking, pop it. Just don't get sensitive when I talk back."

But on Thursday night, the talk came from the line of scrimmage, where Colorado straight-up dominated Georgia Tech's offensive line, which has been the foundation of its program under Brent Key. It came from the toughness to overcome three major special teams gaffes that could easily have cost them the game. And it came from a final drive led by QB Julian Lewis, who played sparingly last year amidst a redshirt and engineered an eight-play, 75-yard drive inside the final minute on a night where he threw for just 124 yards.

There are no secrets here: After three seasons of unrealized potential, this is a critical year for Sanders' viability as a head coach .

No, this opener was not a work of art. But in terms of toughness and play-calling and having enough players with power conference size and speed at every position, it looked like a real football team instead of a vanity project gone wrong.

"I never flinched, man," Sanders said. "I told several people on the sideline, 'We're going to make it very, very interesting, but we're going to win this game.' That's just the faith I have in these young men. The young men played their butts off. We made some mistakes on special teams, which you can't. But they made it happen. So hats off to them. We beat a really, really good team and a really, really good coaching staff. But our guys were resilient. We didn't have many flights back home in victory [last year]. But this is going to be a wonderful flight."

Coming into the season, Colorado was one of those teams that was hard to pin down. After going 3-9 a year ago, the only thing you could say for sure was that they'd be different with a rebuilt coaching staff and a large grab bag of transfers that looked solid on paper but did not have a lot of star power.

Even when Colorado won nine games in Sanders' second year, it often looked like a dysfunctional fire drill that only worked because of the immense talent he had with Travis Hunter being the best player in college football and his son making plays at quarterback when he wasn't forced to run for his life.

It is hard to say how good this Colorado team can be. But it can only be considered a great sign to go on the road against a legitimate, well-run program like Georgia Tech and win the game by running the ball and stopping the run.

"That's what we've been seeing all of fall camp," Lovo said.

Said linebacker Boo Carter, the Tennessee transfer who came off the edge to block the kick: "Just damn violence, you feel me? That's our main word. Just violence."

Even if Colorado had lost this game, it would have been an edifying night for a program that badly needed to show proof of concept. For three years, we didn't really know what a Coach Prime program would look like without extenuating circumstances or players he brought with him from Jackson State.

Now we can see the formation of something different: A normal football team that played really hard and well enough to get a massive season-opening win.

"We know we're big up front," Sanders said "We know we could be physical. We know these guys can move bodies, so that's what we went with. Thank God. Now we're growing as we mature in this game and understanding one another's strengths and weaknesses. When we get all that together, it's going to be a beautiful thing."

articles.title: FPL gameweek three tips: Who are best Man City players to buy?
articles.summary: BBC Sport FPL expert Gianni Buttice looks at some of the biggest dilemmas facing Fantasy Premier League managers heading into gameweek three.
articles.body:
BBC Sport's FPL expert Gianni Buttice looks at some of the biggest dilemmas facing Fantasy Premier League managers heading into gameweek three.

Should I use a Wildcard or Free Hit this week?

If you do not own Erling Haaland (£15.5m), using a chip to bring him in is much simpler than spending several transfers to fit in the game's most expensive player.

A Wildcard lets you move quickly on trending players, improve team value, and invest heavily in two sides you may not have much exposure to in Manchester City and Chelsea , who face Coventry and Hull at home over the next fortnight.

The Free Hit chip also has an upside, allowing you to avoid the Arsenal versus Chelsea fixture and consider players from Brighton , Newcastle , and Brentford .

Who is this week's best Triple Captain option?

If you are not using a Wildcard or Free Hit, choosing Haaland as your Triple Captain looks a strong option, which I am likely to run with.

Coventry have been among the most defensively vulnerable sides and Manchester City impressed last time out, while their Norway striker has had a clear midweek before Saturday's game at Etihad Stadium.

City also host Ipswich in gameweek seven and Hull in gameweek 16, but both fixtures fall during heavy Champions League congestion.

Bruno Fernandes (£12.0m) faces Coventry at Old Trafford in gameweek 14, although that also comes in a run of three matches in seven days.

Cherki, Foden, Gvardiol - who are Man City's best assets?

Rayan Cherki (£7.7m) is this week's most-bought player, with two price rises already. After his impressive last outing, he is the standout midfield pick.

Phil Foden (£7.0m) is also worth considering, with stronger underlying expected data than Cherki over the first two games, while Elliot Anderson (£6.4m) looks a solid long-term hold.

Cherki and Foden may become minutes risks later in the season, especially after the deadline-day signing of Enzo Fernández (£6.9m). In defence, Josko Gvardiol (£5.6m) is the best option.

The half-time substitution of Christos Tzolis against Aston Villa was a concern for owners.

We saw in gameweek one how dangerous he can be and many expect him to be first choice this season, albeit subject to early substitutions.

He's far from a hard sell though and arguably a comfortable hold at £6.5m.

Should I look to switch Fernandes with Palmer or Saka?

Manchester United captain Fernandes is close to the ideal FPL asset: talismanic, takes set-pieces, rarely injured or substituted, and a reliable scorer.

He is a stronger option than Cole Palmer (£9.6m) or Bukayo Saka (£9.5m), but he is also significantly more expensive.

Because captaincy is so important, look ahead. if you are unlikely to captain Fernandes soon, but would give the armband to Palmer or Saka, the switch is worth considering.

It's also worth noting there are plenty of other good assets at Chelsea and Arsenal , whereas Fernandes is in a league of his own at United.

Should I sign someone who joined at the end of the transfer window?

It is easy to be tempted by a new signing, but I would wait at least a week before buying anyone who has only just joined.

Most are unlikely to start this weekend and may be limited to cameo appearances. If they impress on debut, you can react then.

To name a few, I will be closely monitoring Daniel Munoz (£5.4m), Bradley Barcola (£8.0m), Jack Grealish (£6.5m), and the impact Fernandez will have on the minutes of other Manchester City midfielders.

articles.title: Neymar ataca a los trabajadores del Santos tras romperse: "Un trabajo de mierda"
articles.standfirst: Neymar responsabiliza a los jardineros del Vila Belmiro del mal estado del césped que provocó su lesión muscular
articles.summary: Neymar responsabiliza a los jardineros del Vila Belmiro del mal estado del césped que provocó su lesión muscular
articles.body: Neymar criticó duramente el estado del césped del Estadio Urbano Caldeira (popularmente conocido como Vila Belmiro) tras lesionarse ante el Palmeiras, señalando la intervención sobre el campo de los empleados de su club realizada la víspera del encuentro. El futbolista brasileño de 34 años se desató en su 'stories' de Instagram contra los jardineros tras sufrir una lesión muscular en el muslo durante el partido de cuartos de final de la Copa de Brasil que Santos y Palmeiras empataron 0-0. La lesión se produjo cerca del descanso, cuando Neymar sintió una molestia en el muslo. El delantero se dirigió al vestuario entre lágrimas y finalmente no regresó para la segunda parte, siendo sustituido por Rony. "Quería felicitar al responsable del campo de Vila Belmiro. Ayer fue el peor césped que el Vila ha tenido jamás, lleno de baches, porque realizaron una descompactación un día antes del partido. ¡Increíble!", compartió indignado. Neymar subrayó que "además de jugar contra el rival, jugamos contra el campo... y encima tenemos que hacer más esfuerzo al arrancar y frenar durante la carrera porque el terreno está irregular". "No fue casualidad que tres jugadores sufrieran molestias en el primer tiempo... Felicidades... un trabajo de mierda", sentenció. Sobre el estado de su lesión Neymar aclaró que "lamentablemente sentí una molestia en el muslo; me haré pruebas y espero que no sea nada. Seguimos con la cabeza en alto y enfocados en el proceso".

articles.title: 'Serving country against biological clock': Spain to fund egg freezing for women football players; what does it mean?
articles.summary: Off the field News: Spain's football federation is preparing to pay for egg-freezing procedure for its leading women footballers, in a move aimed at helping players balan.
articles.body: Spain's football federation is preparing to pay for egg-freezing procedure for its leading women footballers, in a move aimed at helping players balance motherhood with careers at the highest level.According to a report by EL Pais, the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) is finalising an agreement with a fertility clinic that will allow members of the Spain women's team to undergo egg vitrification. The agreement is expected to be announced later this month, while discussions continue over the exact terms and costs.The move comes as more women athletes face the challenge of fitting pregnancy into long sporting careers. A football career can continue into a player's thirties, but pregnancy often means several months away from training and competition, and returning to the highest level can be difficult.Players raised the issue with the federationFormer Spain captain Alexia Putellas said the team's captains had discussed the issue with the federation and welcomed the proposal."The federation understands that you are serving your country against your biological clock, that you cannot stop and cannot be a mother because you need your body to work," Putellas was quoted as saying by EL Pais."The group of captains had a concern because it is very important for a player to experience World Cups, but that means that those of us who have the desire to become mothers do not find it easy to fit it in."The federation has not yet confirmed whether it will cover the full treatment, only the egg preservation process, or also the egg retrieval procedure.What egg freezing means for elite athletesSports medicine specialist Eva Ferrer said egg vitrification has become a topic of discussion in women's football only over the past couple of years.She explained that there is still limited research on how ovarian stimulation affects athletes. "There are not enough studies on how the treatment [ovarian stimulation] could affect, for example, the joints or soft tissue," Ferrer said as quoted by EL Pais.She added that training may need to be adjusted during treatment to reduce the risk of injury. She also said the medications used during the process must be declared through a Therapeutic Use Exemption (TUE) so athletes do not face anti-doping issues.The treatment usually lasts about two weeks. During that period, the player injects hormonal medication to stimulate the ovaries so multiple eggs mature instead of one. Doctors then retrieve the eggs through a procedure performed under sedation.After the procedure, players may experience bleeding, discomfort, swelling, fluid retention, migraines and lower energy levels while the ovaries recover. Clinics generally recommend collecting around 10 oocytes, though the process can be repeated if needed.Gynecologist Rebeca Beguería said elite athletes do not return to peak physical condition immediately after treatment."The medical protocol states that normal life can be resumed, but for a high-performance athlete these are days when you do not perform at the same level: you will not run as fast or at the same intensity," she told EL Pais.She added that players face a greater risk of injury and abdominal damage during recovery."Your body's blood is redistributed; it is concentrated there; the abdomen and chest are more swollen, there is a tendency to migraines and fluid retention."Beguería also pointed out that while egg freezing helps players delay pregnancy, it does not remove the medical risks associated with becoming pregnant at an older age."Medically, the recommendation is that women get pregnant as early as possible, because biologically we are designed to be mothers by, at most, age 35 and we have extended that."No clear rules yet in women's footballThe proposal has also highlighted the lack of regulations around fertility treatment in professional women's football.Lawyer Tania Tejeira wrote in an opinion piece in Palco23 that neither FIFA nor UEFA currently has a specific protocol covering treatments such as egg freezing or other assisted reproductive technologies, despite more players choosing these options.At present, the main international guidance comes from the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA), which requires medications used during fertility treatment to be reviewed and, where necessary, approved through a Therapeutic Use Exemption.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: FA Cup: From playing with Marcus Rashford at Man Utd to non-league & new career
articles.summary: Ten years after lining up with Marcus Rashford for Manchester United, Joe Riley tells BBC Sport about his new career - and why he does not miss full-time football.
articles.body:
A Tuesday night in Workington in late August and Joe Riley leads his Warrington Rylands team-mates out for a match at the Fibrus Community Stadium in the seventh tier of English football.

Rylands race into a 2-0 lead in Cumbria before losing 3-2 after having two players sent off in a chaotic Northern Premier League Premier Division encounter played in front of 638 supporters.

"A few years back I wouldn't speak for 24 hours if I lost," says Riley, whose side host Hyde United in the first qualifying round of the FA Cup on Saturday (15:00 BST).

"Now if we lose, it's not ideal, but there's always another game around the corner."

It is 10 years since Riley, then aged 19, started at left-back for injury-hit Manchester United against Danish side Midtjylland in the Europa League at Old Trafford, the same match Marcus Rashford also made his first start for the club.

While Rashford has gone on to rack up more than 400 club appearances and earn 78 England caps since scoring two in that emphatic 5-1 win , external a decade ago, Riley left United at 21 with two first-team appearances to his name - and drifted down the leagues after bad luck with injuries.

While recovering from one injury too many at League Two Walsall, he started studying for a new career.

Now aged 29, he sells life insurance, income protection, critical illness and injury cover as a financial protection advisor - while playing non-league football.

"I lived with Scott McTominay for six years, and Marcus and I also came through the academy together," Riley tells BBC Sport.

"Of course I would have liked to have played more games for United but things didn't work out like that.

"I don't dwell on the past - I'm just happy that it happened. I've now got my foot in the door for the next chapter of my life. I'm progressing with another career that's setting me up for the rest of my life."

'I knew I wouldn't play for United again'

Riley grew up in Lytham, Lancashire, and joined United at the age of six.

He went on to play for the under-18s with Rashford, Scotland midfielder McTominay, now at Napoli, and England goalkeeper Dean Henderson, who is at Crystal Palace.

It was while Riley was playing regularly for the under-21s, aged 19, that he - and 18-year-old Rashford - got their big break in February 2016 under Louis van Gaal.

Having come on as a substitute in a 3-0 win at Shrewsbury Town in the fifth round of the FA Cup three days earlier, Riley was named in the starting line-up for a Europa League last-32 tie with Midtjylland, along with Rashford.

United had lost the first leg in Denmark 2-1 and, missing several key players through injury, were in danger of going out of Europe.

England forward Wayne Rooney was among those out receiving treatment along with goalkeeper David de Gea, winger Antonio Valencia and defender Chris Smalling.

"The day before the game Van Gaal stuck the starting XI on a board at a team meeting," recalls Riley.

The young player carefully went down the list of familiar names.

Michael Carrick, Daley Blind, Juan Mata, Jesse Lingard, Memphis Depay... Joe Riley!

"I remember thinking: 'Oh my God'. It was a dream come true."

Riley's mum, Derren, and sister, Sophie, were in the 58,609 crowd at Old Trafford to watch him play 79 minutes.

By the time United's No 49 received a standing ovation when he was replaced by Argentina left-back Marcos Rojo, who was returning after three months out with a dislocated shoulder, Van Gaal's side were leading 3-1 on the night (4-3 agg), before scoring a further two late goals to book a last-16 European tie with Liverpool.

"I had a really good game but I do remember thinking that could be my last for the first team, because the likes of Rojo and Luke Shaw were working their way back from injuries," he says.

While Rashford went on to play several more times that season, including United's FA Cup final win over Crystal Palace at Wembley, Riley did not appear again for the senior side.

He continued to train with the first team even after Van Gaal was sacked and replaced by Jose Mourinho in May 2016, and was named captain of the under-23s.

By 2017, however, injuries were already starting to disrupt his career.

A damaged hamstring delayed a loan move to Sheffield United and, when the player did eventually arrive at Bramall Lane, the loan was cut short after he dislocated his shoulder.

Riley's 15 years at United ended on 25 May 2018, two years after that magical night against Midtjylland.

While former under-18s team-mate Rashford was preparing to go to the World Cup in Russia with England, Riley joined League One Bradford City on a two-year contract.

'I'm loving life away from full-time football'

Riley's two years with the Bantams included 10 months out with an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury. Then there was a long-standing foot issue soon after joining Walsall in 2022, following an injury-free two seasons at League Two Carlisle.

"It took six months to find out what was wrong with my foot and then another three months to recover after surgery," says Riley.

Riley started making plans for life after football in case he was forced to retire early because of injury.

"It was getting to the point of wondering if I was ever going to be able to play again because this pain was in my foot and nobody could find it. If you can't find something, how do you fix it?"

By the time specialists discovered the cause was floating bone fragments, Riley was studying for a new career in financial services.

Today, he works for a company in Sale, near Manchester, after bringing the curtain down on his full-time playing career after spells in the National League with Fylde and Tamworth.

"I'm loving it," adds Riley about his career in finance protection.

"Moving from full-time football to part-time was something I once feared, like many players do. Instead my job is rewarding, while I joined Warrington Rylands in the summer - a club I thoroughly enjoy being at.

"I've started my exams to become a wealth manager to help with investments and pensions.

"I don't want to play full-time again. Even if an opportunity arose, I'm too far down the road in terms of preparing for life away from football."

Riley's mum can be seen at Warrington Rylands matches supporting her son, just as she did on that cold February Thursday night at Old Trafford all those years ago.

"I will forever be grateful to Manchester United," says Riley, who is engaged to be married to Elizabeth, his partner for the past seven years, next summer in the south of France.

"United turned me into the person I am today - I've got them to thank for that."

And what about Rashford. Is he still in touch with his former academy team-mate?

"I don't have Marcus' number so we don't message. If I bumped into him, I've no doubt it would be just the same as all those years ago when we were growing up together.

"I saw [United boss] Michael Carrick in Portugal this summer and we had a really good chat."

Although he has moved on with his life, Riley does have one regret from his time with United.

Having played a small part in their triumphant 2016 FA Cup campaign, the young United substitute at Shrewsbury wishes he had pressed the club for a winners' medal.

"Had I done so then I probably would have received one," he says.

"I didn't go to Wembley because I wasn't in the squad for the final. At the time I was young and naive, thinking I'd have plenty more opportunities to get a medal.

"In the end I only got to play two first-team games for Manchester United. No-one though will ever be able to take those memories away from me."

articles.title: Driouech y Antañón se estrenaron en San Sebastián
articles.standfirst: Primeros minutos para ambos esta temporada
articles.summary: Primeros minutos para ambos esta temporada
articles.body: Dos nuevos debutantes célticos en el partido ante la Real Sociedad. Couhaib Driouech, penúltimo fichaje del verano, se estrenó con la elástica celeste, y Andrés Antañón lo hizo con el primer equipo esta temporada, ya que hasta la fecha había participado en los tres encuentros del Celta Fortuna en Segunda. Claudio Giráldez ya ha utilizado a 22 futbolistas. Couhaib Driouech muestra su satisfacción: “Estoy muy contento. He esperado varias semanas para que llegase este momento y estoy muy contento de ser parte del equipo y de ya tener minutos”. El ex de PSV valora el empate ante la Real Sociedad: “Fue un partido difícil en el que defendimos bien. Ellos hicieron ocasiones y en la segunda parte las tuvimos nosotros para marcar. Creo que que es justo el 0-0”. Andrés Antañón también estaba satisfecho con el debut esta temporada y algo menos con el resultado: “En lo personal muy contento por salir de inicio pero nos vamos con la pena de no llevarnos los tres puntos que creo que por momentos hemos merecido. También tenemos que valorar un punto en un campo tan complicado como este. Hay que valorarlo, además contra un equipazo como es la Real Sociedad que en muchos momentos del partido te embotella, te hace estar en bloque bajo”.

articles.summary: Henry cree que si el Liverpool aprovecha correctamente las fortalezas de Barcola, el jugador de 125 millones podría ser decisivo en la Premier
articles.body: Thierry Henry, exjugador del F.C. Barcelona que triunfa como comentarista televisivo, ha advertido al Liverpool sobre el estelar fichaje de Bradley Barcola. Los 'reds' han pagado 145 millones de euros al PSG por el delantero francés, que ha firmado hasta 2031 convirtiéndose en el segundo fichaje más caro de la historia del Liverpool. "La clave con Barcola es: ¿Cómo lo vas a utilizar? ¿Puedes generar situaciones de uno contra uno? Además: ¿Puedes involucrarlo en contraataques? Porque es rápido como el demonio", comentó el exfutbolista francés en 'Sky Sports'. Thierry Henry advierte a Iraola y al Liverpool que no deben sobrecargar a Barbala con tareas defensivas que mermen su condiciones ofensivas: "¿Tiene que defender más que atacar? Eso podría ser contraproducente para él". "Lo último que diría es que necesita mejorar un poco Barcola es la finalización. Si lo consigue, muchos equipos tendrán problemas para frenarlo", apuntó el exseleccionador sub-21 de Francia. Jamie Carragher, leyenda del Liverpool, agregó que Barcola aporta a la Premier League ese toque de magia tan necesario, si bien cuestionó el equilibrio general de la plantilla del Liverpool.

articles.title: London City Lionesses v Man Utd: Mary Earps eyes reunion on WSL comeback
articles.summary: Mary Earps is back in the Women's Super League and hopes to mark her return by facing former club Manchester United.
articles.body:
Mary Earps is no stranger to the Women's Super League and hopes to mark her return with a match against her former club.

The new London City Lionesses goalkeeper felt it was "meant to be" that her potential debut could come against Manchester United.

During the peak of her career, she spent five seasons at United, becoming England number one and twice being named Fifa's goalkeeper of the year.

After a spell at Paris St-Germain, Earps wants to return to England on a high in Friday's season opener (19:00 BST) and will no doubt find herself in the limelight again.

"I got a nice reception at Old Trafford [in the Women's Champions League last season] and it meant a great deal to me at that time," Earps told BBC Sport.

"United has changed a lot since I left, but I spent five wonderful years there and I made amazing memories.

"I won an FA Cup and met a lot of incredible people. I know the fans don't change - they are still as hardcore as ever."

The 33-year-old made more than 100 appearances for United and helped them win their first major trophy in 2024.

She also played a crucial role in England's victory at Euro 2022 and their route to the 2023 World Cup final while she was at United.

That earned her many individual accolades, including BBC Sports Personality of the Year in 2023 and she became one of the country's most recognised and influential players.

However last November, her book caused controversy and dominated headlines in the media for several weeks.

Even so, Earps received a warm applause when she faced United with PSG last season and the mural painted of her outside Old Trafford remains.

As she prepares to face her former club again, what does Earps want to achieve at London City and why was it time to return home?

Media Day Diaries: Inside London City Lionesses

How to follow women's football with BBC Sport this season

Earps spent two years at PSG and made 22 appearances in the Premiere Ligue last season.

She left United in search of Champions League football and silverware, but was also able to take a break from the limelight in England.

That attention rose again last year following the release of her book, but Earps is thankful for the experiences she gained in Paris.

"I'm grateful for all the amazing love and support that I've had over the years, but it was nice to be away," said Earps.

"PSG is a great club. Getting to experience the Parc des Princes, the French food, the Parisian way of life and the language - I think it was good for me.

"I'm an intense person, especially when I'm on the pitch, so it was good for me to be able to take a period of reflection away from the craziness in England.

"But that being said, I'm incredibly grateful for this platform that I've been given so it's not a complaint. I went away to push myself out of my comfort zone."

However, upon the expiry of her contract, Earps craved a return to England where she could experience WSL atmospheres once again.

"Of course, there's always things that you miss. I'm very, very happy to be home," she added.

"I missed the English football culture - the way you feel when you walk into a stadium, the electricity of the crowd, the feeling around women's football in this country.

"I knew I was probably going to miss that going away which is why I'm so excited to be back. Distance makes the heart grow fonder."

Earps is one of the big-name players to join London City this summer, joining two-time Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas and Spain defender Mapi Leon at the club.

She started both of London City's past two pre-season matches but knows she faces a battle to take the number-one shirt given fellow goalkeeper Elene Lete impressed last term.

"The reality of it is that I've been here a few weeks and I'm trying to earn my place in the team every single day," said Earps.

"Elene did a great job last year and it won't be easy between us to see who starts. I think that is another great thing about being part of a fantastic squad.

"I just want to contribute to the team's success and hopefully that is playing a lot of games and being a part of their history in some small way."

Earps announced her international retirement in 2025 but does not intend to call quits on her club career any time soon.

She signed a two-year deal with London City and believes she can still improve as the club plots a course up the WSL table.

"I want to continue to play at the highest level, to win at the highest level for as long as possible and to be a part of something special," said Earps.

"I really do believe that London City will go on to do great things for a long time. They want to be the best in class and world-leading.

"That is something that I'm always pushing to be - to be the best version of myself as a player and a person every day.

"It's a great place to be for me to max out on whatever potential I have left. The moment that I don't think I can learn any more, I won't continue to play.

"I still feel like I've got a lot to give and hopefully there's some fantastic days around the corner. I'm really looking forward to this chapter."

articles.title: Manchester United latest: Michael Carrick happy with transfer business and convinced that his squad has improved after summer window
articles.summary: Manchester United finished the transfer window with a lower net spent then new boys Coventry and Ipswich, but Carrick still believes his squad has gotten stronger; watch Everton vs Man Utd live on Super Sunday from 1pm on Sunday, kick-off 2pm
articles.body:
United spent the summer window focusing on a midfield overhaul, securing the signings of Andrey Santos from Chelsea , Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa and Carlos Baleba from Brighton . Goalkeeper Karl Darlow also joined the club on a free transfer from Leeds.

The Red Devils' net spend across the transfer window finished at £118m, less than the likes of newly promoted Ipswich and Coventry and Gary Neville was adamant that United need to invest in their defence before the end of the window.

However, despite failing to do so, Carrick is confident in the strength of his squad for the remainder of the season.

"I think we've brought some really good players into the football club, and improved the squad in different ways, individually but collectively," Carrick said during a charity golf day for his foundation.

"I think we've grown. You go into the window and when you come out of it, you want to be stronger than you were at the start. I'm convinced we are that.

"Transfer windows are never straightforward and this window in particular has been challenging for different reasons. There's a lot of money being spent in and around the league itself, and I think we've made the most of the situation that we've found ourselves in.

"That's the world we live in. Teams at certain points are going to spend a lot of money. Sometimes it's going to be more than what we spend, sometimes maybe not. We've got to make the most of what we can and understand where we're at. I think we're a very good team, we want to keep getting better."

Bounce-back against Ipswich showed United's 'character'

Carrick couldn't have asked for a worse start to the new season as his side were left humiliated by newly promoted Hull City on the opening weekend. However, after surviving an early scare, they responded with an emphatic 5-2 victory over Ipswich Town in their first home game of the campaign.

The former Red Devils midfielder was keen to point out the courage of his squad for bouncing back from such a disappointment, saying it gives him plenty of encouragement moving forward.

"Since I came back really and we got the group together, we've lost a couple of games, we've had some setbacks, but the way the boys have dealt with it gives us a lot of courage moving forward," Carrick said.

"At some point you're going to have things that go against you. Whether that's a game or a moment in games, and I've talked about it this week. I think the response that we showed and the confidence the boys had, that's when you find out quite a bit about what you are as a group.

"I thought we did a lot of good things in the first half. We had a few minutes when it didn't go well for us, we took that into the second half and played some really good football.

"A lot of people talk about the goals and the results in the end, but I think the mentality is what pleased us the most. It gives us a lot of encouragement moving forward."

'He's set the example' - Carrick waxes lyrical on Bruno

Despite several strong performers against Ipswich, the main headlines once again centred around Bruno Fernandes.

The PFA Player of the Year opened his account for the campaign with his third hat-trick for the club and another sublime assist for Bryan Mbeumo's goal.

The heroics from Fernandes led to Gary Neville labelling the club captain as the best signing post-Sir Alex Ferguson, and Carrick struggled to find his own superlatives for the Portugal international.

"I've spoken an awful lot about Bruno, and I think it just shows what he can do," Carrick added.

"I think how important he is for us, and the impact that he has. He's done it over such a long period of time and since we've started working together again, I think he's been nothing but positive all the way through.

"He's set the example every day. He trains well, his attitude is spot-on, he's desperate to win, he's desperate to do well, and then he puts in performances like that. Bruno is the first to admit it's a team game and I thought there were other individuals in the team that had a fantastic afternoon.

"Bruno gets the headlines, and I understand why. Rightly so, because the quality of his moments was pretty special at the weekend. I'm definitely sure there will be more of them as the season goes on."

articles.title: El Liverpool 'castiga' sin Champions a Chiesa y Endo y el Bayern se deja fuera de la lista a Karl
articles.standfirst: El Tottenham, por su parte, se ha cargado a Richarlison de la lista de la Premier
articles.summary: El Tottenham, por su parte, se ha cargado a Richarlison de la lista de la Premier
articles.body: La confirmación oficial de las listas de la Champions League para la Fase Liga suele deparar importantes ausencias. Esta temporada, sin embargo, no ha habido tantas. La más llamativa, probablemente, sea la de Ferland Mendy. Su fecha de recuperación es una incógnita. El lateral izquierdo del Real Madrid continúa recuperándose de la rotura que sufrió en el tendón del recto femoral de su pierna derecha. En el Barcelona se entiende la ausencia de Roony Bardghji, que estará alrededor de seis meses de baja. 'Hansi' Flick, en su lugar, ha apostado por incluir a los prometedores Hamza Abdelkarim, Jesse Bisiwu y Brian Fariñas. Fuera del Real Madrid, las dos ausencias más mediáticas, probablemente, sean las del Liverpool. Andoni Iraola ha dejado fuera de la lista a Federico Chiesa y Wataru Endo. Ha preferido incluir a jugadores como Hugo Ekitike, Giovanni Leoni y Conor Bradley, que salen de lesiones de larga duración y están ultimando su 'puesta a punto'. "El Liverpool tiene dos jugadores en la plantilla que nunca van a jugar. Chiesa y Endo es como si nunca fueran a tocar un balón. A Endo se le debería haber dado salida. Lo ha hecho muy bien, es una especie de héroe de culto", aseguró Jamie Carragher, excapitán 'red', en 'Sky Sports'. En el Aston Villa, sin salir de la Premier, llama la atención la ausencia de Taylor Harwood-Bellis. Especialmente porque los de Unai Emery acaban de pagar 29,2 millones de euros al Southampton por el central inglés, de 24 años. En el Bayern sorprende la ausencia de Lennart Karl. Eso no significa, sin embargo, que el talentoso mediapunta/extremo alemán no vaya a jugar la Champions. Podría ser incluido en cualquier momento -lo será con total seguridad- en la 'lista B' al ser un jugador nacido después de enero de 2005 (es de 2008) y haber jugado durante, al menos, dos temporadas consecutivas en el Bayern después de haber cumplido los 15 años. No deja, sin embargo, de ser llamativo. Una situación idéntica a la que están viviendo en el Manchester United tanto Leny Yoro como Kobbie Mainoo. Ningundo de los dos ha sido confirmado en la lista 'A'... pero nadie duda de que serán incluidos en la 'B'. Es una estrategia que permite a los clubes inscribir a más jugadores que no se hayan formado en su cantera. El que se ha llevado un 'palo doble' es Folarin Balogun. A su frustrado fichaje por el Everton se suma que el Mónaco le ha dejado fuera de la lista, en este caso, de la Conference League. En esta ocasión no hay red, ni paracaídas... ni lista 'B'. Deberá esperar hasta enero, al menos, para participar en la Europa. Su futuro incierto -continúa recuperándose de la lesión que sufrió en el Mundial- y la competencia con Paris Brunner, Ansu Fati, Matthis Abline, Mika Biereth y Takumi Minamino le ha dejado fuera. El que se ha tenido que 'abrir la cabeza' para confeccionar su lista para la Champions es Cesc Fàbregas. Ha podido incluir a sus dos últimas incorporaciones, Moise Kean y el español Robert Sánchez, pero ha tenido que dejar fuera hasta a seis jugadores de la primera plantilla: Mauro Vigorito, Edoardo Goldaniga, Willy Kambwala, Maxence Caqueret, Adrian Lahdo y Jayden Addai. En Italia, el Nápoles ha excluido a Luca Marianucci y Giovane y la Roma de Gasperini ha hecho lo propio con Anass Salah-Eddine y Devis Vázquez. Ha incluido, en cambio, al prometedor Antonio Arena (2009). El Oporto de Francesco Farioli también se ha visto obligado a hacer 'encaje de bolillos'. Los 'dragones' han sacado de la lista a Dominik Prpic, su cuarta opción para el eje de la defensa, y al brasileño Gabriel Mec. Recién llegado desde el Shakhtar Donetsk, la idea es no forzar su adaptación a Portugal. El Tottenham no compite en Champions esta temporada, pero ha tenido que confeccionar su lista para la Premier. La selección entregada por Roberto de Zerbi deja un bombazo: Richarlison no figura entre los elegidos. La idea inicial es que el atacante brasileño, de 29 años, abandonara el Tottenham para regresar al Everton antes del cierre del mercado. La operación, sin embargo, no cuajó. Ahora los 'Spurs' confían en encontrarle salida en alguno de los mercados que continúan abiertos (Arabia Saudí y Turquía). De lo contrario, Richarlison no podrá volver a jugar... hasta enero.

articles.title: Mourinho y Parrott: del balón del debut en la Premier a su reencuentro en LaLiga siete años después
articles.standfirst: El portugués fue quien le dio la alternativa al irlandés del Betis en su etapa en el Tottenham
articles.summary: El portugués fue quien le dio la alternativa al irlandés del Betis en su etapa en el Tottenham
articles.body: El Estadio de La Cartuja vivirá esta noche muchos reencuentros. Por ejemplo, el de Pellegrini y Mourinho, una vez zanjada públicamente por ambos la polémica surgida hace más de una década por una desafortunada frase del portugués; los de Diego Llorente, Álvaro Fidalgo e Isco Alarcón con el club al que pertenecieron; o los de Fran García y Dani Ceballos con quienes, hasta hace poco más de un par de meses, eran sus compañeros de equipo. Pero también habrá oportunidad de que se crucen en la banda dos viejos conocidos: José Mourinho y Troy Parrott. Hace casi siete años, el actual técnico del Real Madrid y el delantero irlandés, recién llegado al Betis, compartieron un momento muy especial en Inglaterra. El portugués fue uno de los entrenadores que acompañó al nuevo goleador verdiblanco en sus primeros pasos en la élite y protagonizaron juntos una curiosa historia que todavía hoy guarda un significado especial para Parrott. Ocurrió el 7 de diciembre de 2019, pocas semanas después de la llegada de Mou al banquillo del Tottenham, en un partido en el que los Spurs golearon por 5-0 al Burnley y que supuso el debut de Troy en la Premier League, con sólo 17 años de edad, sustituyendo a Dele Alli en los minutos finales. El irlandés, que se presentaba como una de las joyas de la cantera del conjunto londinense y como el heredero natural de Harry Kane, ya había tenido la oportunidad de estrenarse con el primer equipo. Había jugado pocos meses antes más de una hora de partido, de la mano de Mauricio Pochettino, frente al Colchester United en una eliminatoria de la EFL Cup. Pero fue con Mourinho, sustituto del argentino en la dirección técnica de los Spurs, con quien pudo cumplir el sueño de debutar en la Premier, una estreno que quedó para el recuerdo por un balón que terminó ocupando un lugar especial en la casa de la madre de Troy. En la goleada del Tottenham ante el Burnley, el surcoreano Heung-min Son marcó un de los tantos más espectaculares de su carrera. Un impresionante eslalon sorteando rivales hasta encontrar la portería. Como premio, y pese a que Kane había rozado el triplete con dos dianas, quiso llevarse la pelota a casa. Pero ahí apareció Mourinho, acercándose al mediapunta para pedírsela porque entendía que tendría un significado mucho más especial para Parrott. Se acercó al irlandés, se la regaló y ambos se fundieron en un abrazo. Un gesto que, pese al tiempo transcurrido, el delantero bético no ha olvidado. "A veces el balón es para el jugador que marca un 'hat-trick'. Creo que tiene mucho más significado para un chico de 17 años", explicó Mourinho en ese momento sobre su decisión. Una semana antes, Parrott estaba jugando la Youth League con futbolistas de su edad. Y de repente, compartía vestuario y terreno de juego con las estrellas del Tottenham en la Premier, incluido el argentino Giovani Lo Celso, compañero suyo hoy en el vestuario del Betis. Aquel balón viajó después a Dublín, a la casa familiar de un futbolista que sueña ahora con hacer carrera en LaLiga. La relación entre José y Troy, sin embargo, fue mucho más allá de aquel gesto. Mourinho veía potencial en el joven delantero, pero también trató de frenar las expectativas que comenzaban a generarse a su alrededor. Con Kane lesionado y parte de la afición reclamando más minutos para el canterano, el técnico portugués dejó claro públicamente que todavía tenía camino por recorrer. "Todavía no es un jugador hecho", llegó a decir sobre Parrott, al que definió como "un privilegiado" por tener la oportunidad de entrenarse habitualmente con el primer equipo siendo prácticamente un juvenil. Mourinho también le reclamó más cuando bajaba a jugar con el equipo sub-23, convencido de que debía demostrar sobre el césped por qué era uno de los elegidos para trabajar con los mayores. El tiempo ha terminado dando otra perspectiva a Parrott de aquellos meses. El delantero ha reconocido posteriormente que entonces se sentía preparado para jugar regularmente en la Premier, aunque ahora entiende que todavía le faltaba recorrido, especialmente desde el punto de vista físico. "Me sentía preparado, pero creo que no lo estaba", admitió el delantero irlandés en una extensa e interesante entrevista concedida a Miguel Delaney para The Independent en febrero de este mismo año, cuando defendía los colores del AZ Alkmaar. También desveló parte del trabajo que Mourinho realizó con él durante su etapa en Londres. Pese a dirigir a un vestuario repleto de estrellas, el portugués dedicaba tiempo al joven atacante para corregir movimientos y enseñarle dónde debía aparecer dentro del área. Y tenía el mejor ejemplo posible a pocos metros. "Sacaba tiempo para intentar ayudarme a mejorar, para enseñarme qué posiciones debía ocupar, utilizando a Harry Kane como referencia", recordó Parrott sobre Mourinho. Una exigencia que se quedaba principalmente sobre el césped: "En el campo sí era exigente. Fuera de él era una persona con muy buen carácter". Parrott terminó abandonando el Tottenham después de varias cesiones y encontró en los Países Bajos el escenario ideal para relanzar su carrera. Sus caminos y los de Mourinho volvieron a cruzarse fugazmente durante la etapa del portugués en el Fenerbahçe, después de un partido frente al AZ Alkmaar, cuando ambos mantuvieron una conversación. Esta noche volverán a verse, ahora en LaLiga y como adversarios. Mourinho tendrá enfrente a un futbolista muy distinto de aquel adolescente de 17 años que intentaba abrirse paso entre las estrellas del Tottenham. Parrott se encontrará de nuevo con uno de los técnicos que marcaron sus primeros pasos en la élite. El mismo que un día le pidió el balón a Son para regalárselo como recuerdo de su estreno en la Premier.

articles.summary: El noruego es la única baja rojiblanca en la sesión previa a viajar a Bilbao. La Araña, más relajado, bromeó con varios compañeros.

Espera el Athletic, espera San Mamés, y la Araña es uno de los recursos que tiene Simeone para asaltar la Catedral. Una alineación en la que los jugadores ofensivos fueron Kang-in, Baena, Giuliano y Lookman, que apuntan a repetir pese a la llegada del último refuerzo. articles.title: Marco Asensio desmiente las fake news sobre su salud: "Creo que tengo que intervenir"
articles.standfirst: El mallorquín, que milita en el Fenerbahçe, lanza un comunicado poniendo fin a las informaciones que decían que se tenía que someter a una operación. "Pronto estaré en el equipo"
articles.summary: El mallorquín, que milita en el Fenerbahçe, lanza un comunicado poniendo fin a las informaciones que decían que se tenía que someter a una operación. "Pronto estaré en el equipo"
articles.body: El Fenerbahçe vive una semana movida a dos días de uno de los partidos más importantes del curso, el derbi ante el Besiktas (sábado, Chobani Stadı, 4ª jornada de la Süper Lig). En pleno revuelo por unas informaciones que apuntaban a una lesión seria de rodilla y una posible operación, Marco Asensio ha decidido dar la cara personalmente a través de la web oficial del club para zanjar cualquier duda sobre su estado físico. El español fue tajante desde el primer momento: "Desmiento categóricamente las noticias que han salido", aseguró, dejando claro que no existe ningún plan para pasar por el quirófano. El propio jugador reconoció que no suele responder a este tipo de informaciones que considera falsas, pero que en esta ocasión, al tratarse de su salud y de la ilusión de toda la afición amarilla, sentía la necesidad de pronunciarse directamente. Lejos de ratificar problemas físicos, Asensio quiso todo lo contrario: aportar buenas noticias sobre su recuperación. El mallorquín explicó que ya ha comenzado a entrenar de forma progresiva sobre el césped y que su reincorporación al grupo llegará "muy pronto", aunque sin confirmar si estará disponible ya para el derbi de este mismo sábado. El centrocampista fue más allá y lanzó un dardo velado hacia quienes, en su opinión, buscan "alterar la estabilidad" del vestuario justo en la previa de una cita tan señalada para el conjunto de Estambul. El futbolista aprovechó además su comparecencia para poner en valor el gran arranque de temporada del Fenerbahçe, remarcando el regreso del club a la Champions League después de 18 años de ausencia, y pidió a la afición que llene el estadio y respalde al equipo hasta el final en el duelo ante su eterno rival. "Hola a todos los hinchas del Fenerbahçe. Estoy aquí para desmentir las últimas noticias de que me tengo que operar. Como sabéis, no suelo responder a este tipo de noticias falsas. Sin embargo, cuando se trata de mi salud y de la emoción de todos los aficionados del Fenerbahçe, creo que tengo que intervenir. Por lo tanto, desmiento totalmente las noticias que han salido. He empezado poco a poco en el campo. Muy pronto estaré con el equipo. Llevo mucho tiempo aquí. Entiendo que hay quienes quieren alterar la estabilidad del equipo. Quedan dos días para un derbi muy importante para nosotros, todo va bien; quiero destacar que volveré al equipo muy pronto. Hemos empezado la temporada muy bien. Fenerbahçe está de nuevo en la Champions League después de 18 años. Hemos cogido un gran impulso positivo. Por eso, todos juntos debemos concentrarnos en el partido contra el Besiktas del sábado. Espero que el estadio esté, como siempre, a tope; animando al equipo y que ganemos este partido. ¡Hasta el final! Gracias por vuestro apoyo de siempre." El comunicado de Marco Asensio ha reforzado la narrativa expuesta con anterioridad por parte de su club, el Fernebahçe, quien señalaba directamente a un periodista acusándole de verter una afirmaciones "completamente falsas y producto de la imaginación" y le "invita" a corregir su información "que induce a error a la opinión pública", en un tema tan "extremadamente sensible como es el estado de salud de un deportista". "No existe ninguna base real en las expresiones que indican que nuestro jugador tiene un problema grave en los ligamentos de la rodilla desde el inicio de la temporada, que corre riesgo de una lesión en el ligamento cruzado, que desea someterse a una operación y que ha hecho tal solicitud a nuestro club", zanja el Fenerbahçe.

articles.title: El 'bajón' de Vermeeren: regresa a la casilla de salida
articles.standfirst: El ex del Atlético vuelve al Amberes, cedido por el Leipzig, para recuperar su mejor nivel
articles.summary: El ex del Atlético vuelve al Amberes, cedido por el Leipzig, para recuperar su mejor nivel
articles.body: La Champions 2023-24 y, en particular, su actuación en la victoria contra el Barcelona (3-2) -gol incluido- 'colocó en el escaparate' a Arthur Vermeeren (Lier, 2005). "El nuevo Iniesta, el nuevo Xavi, el nuevo Busquets...", aseguraba el medio belga 'HLN' al referirse al prometedor mediocentro del Amberes. "No le daré ninguna información porque si se la doy lo ficharía inmediatamente", aseguraba su por entonces entrenador, Mark van Bommel, al ser preguntado por el interés del Barcelona. Paradójicamente, Vermeeren terminó recalando en el Atlético en enero de 2024 a cambio de 20 millones de euros. "Estoy muy contento de ser un jugador de Simeone", reconocía en su presentación. Con 'El Cholo', sin embargo, jugó poco. Apenas disputó cinco partidos (160') antes de marcharse cedido, ese mismo verano, al RB Leipzig. Un préstamo, con opción de compra obligatoria en función del número de partidos disputados, que permitió al Atlético recuperar los 20 kilos que pagó al Amberes. En Leipzig jugó 41 partidos (2.270') y repartió dos asistencias, pero no cuajó. De ahí que los 'toros' decidieran enviarle cedido al Olympique de Marsella el pasado verano. En el Vélodrome tampoco consiguió establecerse como titular. Ni con Roberto de Zerbi... ni con Habib Beye. Cerró el curso con 26 partidos (1.211') y dos pases de gol. Sin sitio de vuelta a Leipzig, Vermeeren ha decidido regresar a la casilla de salida. El internacional belga jugará cedido esta temporada en el Amberes. "Durante su primera etapa en el club, se consolidó como uno de los artífices del doblete. Bienvenido de nuevo, Arthur, y mucha suerte!", presumía el conjunto belga en el anuncio de su incorporación. Vermeeren, que lucirá el dorsal 48, confía en que este 'paso atrás' le permita dar dos hacia adelante en el futuro. "Me alegro de estar de vuelta. Tengo muchas ganas de ayudar al equipo y al club", aseguró a modo de presentación. Con el Amberes ya ganó Liga, Copa y Supercopa en 2023, además de exhibir su mejor versión en ataque: marcó tres goles y repartió ocho asistencias en 66 encuentros. Desde luego que tiempo -sólo tiene 21 años- le sobra.

articles.title: Alexandre Pato consortium's Northampton Town investment approved
articles.summary: The Independent Football Regulator approves investment into the Cobblers by a Brazilian consortium.
articles.body:
A consortium including former AC Milan, Chelsea and Brazil forward Alexandre Pato has had a "proposed shareholding aquisition" of Northampton Town approved by the Independent Football Regulator (IFR) and English Football League (EFL), the League Two club has said.

Sports Alpha Capital (SAC) was previously in discussions about taking over Colchester United earlier this year but decided to pull out of a potential deal following initial talks.

Pato is named by SAC , external as one of its investors, along with Gemcorp Capital, a London-based independent investment management firm.

The size of SAC's proposed shareholding in the Cobblers has not been disclosed at this stage.

The club said that full details regarding the investment, structure and the principal investors involved would be announced upon completion of the deal.

Friday's announcement ended months of speculation, after the club first disclosed it was talking to the "well-funded investment group" in April.

Pato, 37, retired from playing last year. He is best known for his five-and-a-half-year spell at AC Milan where he scored 63 goals in 150 matches and won the Serie A title in the 2010-11 season.

Pre-match, post-match and topical Cobblers content

Northampton chairman Kelvin Thomas said: "This has been a detailed and rigorous process, involving significant scrutiny of the proposed investment, the ownership structure, financial sustainability, and the suitability and financial standing of those involved.

"The successful completion of both the IFR and EFL processes represents an important milestone for the club and should provide supporters and stakeholders with further confidence in the proposed investment and the foundations being put in place for the club's future.

"We would like to thank both the EFL and the IFR for their professionalism, diligence and thoroughness throughout their respective processes.

"As supporters will see from their varied backgrounds, there is a genuine passion for football within the group. A number of the investors have already visited Northampton, spent time at the club and attended matches.

"They will bring a strong blend of football, corporate and financial expertise to the club and with significant Brazilian representation within the group we also hope they might bring a little Brazilian excitement and flair with them.

"Now the regulatory processes have been completed we move towards completing the remaining documentation and finalising the investment. Full details regarding the investment, structure and the principal investors involved will be announced upon completion.

"We thank the fans for their patience, but it is reassuring that these in-depth processes are in place for football."

The deal comes after a difficult year for the League Two side.

The Cobblers suffered relegation to the fourth tier last season, finishing bottom of the League One table. They remain without a win so far in 2026-27.

In April, the club announced a pre-tax loss just short of £3m, with Thomas previously saying that the proposed investment would make the club debt-free.

Northampton appointed Chris Hogg as their manager in May and brought in 13 players during the summer transfer window, including striker Matty Warhurst from Manchester City.

articles.title: La Rosaleda, una asignatura pendiente del Levante
articles.standfirst: De los doce encuentros disputados en Málaga, los granotas han caído en nueve ocasiones
articles.summary: De los doce encuentros disputados en Málaga, los granotas han caído en nueve ocasiones
articles.body: El Levante tiene este fin de semana un examen histórico que superar. Vencer en el estadio de La Rosaleda. El conjunto granota buscará la segunda victoria consecutiva, tras el triunfo de la pasada jornada ante el Real Betis (5-2). El cuadro valenciano ha disputado en Málaga un total de doce encuentros, en partido oficial tanto en Primera y Segunda División, con un global de nueve derrotas y tres empates. La gran mayoría en este siglo. El primer envite disputado entre ambos, se remonta a la temporada 1964/1965, con el Levante en la máxima categoría del fútbol nacional, y donde se midió ante los boquerones en la promoción por la permanencia. En aquel partido, los granotas cayeron por 4-0, previo a un empate a cero en el Ciutat y que supuso su descenso a Segunda. Veinticinco años más tarde, ambos equipos se volvieron a ver las caras en la categoría de plata con una victoria contundente para los andaluces, por 4-1. Aquella temporada, el Levante descendería a Segunda División B, tras concluir en penúltima posición. Ya en este siglo, los granotas encadenaron cinco derrotas seguidss, (2004, 2010, 2012, 2013, 2014), todos ellos en la categoría de oro. En 2014, el equipo dirigido por José Luis Mendilibar, sacó un empate sin goles. Tras una nueva derrota en 2016, por 3-1, el cuadro azulgrana cambió la dinámica, aunque sin poder sumar las tres unidades. En 2017, con Muñiz en el banco, rascó otro empate ante un Málaga que terminó como colista a 23 puntos de la salvación. En 2023 y 2025, en Segunda División, volvieron a repartirse los puntos, 0-0 y 1-1, este último con gol de Pablo Martínez, actual jugador blanquiazul, desde el punto de penalti y que concluiría el curso con el ascenso a Primera División.

articles.title: Harry Kane: Europe's top scorer plays like a midfielder - we asked him to break down his game
articles.summary: Harry Kane was the highest goalscorer in Europe last season, yet he plays like a midfielder. We ask him to break down his game.
articles.body:
As Harry Kane's career has progressed, the 33-year-old has taken an increasingly complete role, popping up to collect the ball as deep as his own box.

Many wonder why a talisman tasked with scoring doesn't spend more time closer to goal, but last season the England and Bayern Munich striker scored 73 goals - the highest tally of his career - while playing deeper than he ever has done.

When I mention this paradox, a grin spreads across his face.

"Until you really understand football and understand what we've been talking about, it's so easy to say 'stay high, you're going to score' but it doesn't work like that," Kane says.

I sat down to speak to Kane about the finer details of his game, shedding light on his unique role.

Watching Kane train, his professionalism is palpable. England's record goalscorer is one of the first out on the pitch. The younger players indulge in playful kick-ups as he watches, engaged in conversation with a member of staff.

From a distance, that makes it easy to confuse him with a coach but, given his role on the pitch, it is a fitting mistake.

Kane's style of play reflects who he is as a person, with those who know him saying he is well-rounded and humble on and off the pitch.

The season is in its infancy but Kane isn't basking in the success of the past 12 months. With only five days of pre-season training under his belt, the England captain completed 90 minutes of Bayern's 2-1 win over Borussia Dortmund to lift the German Super Cup.

As demanding as his roaming role is, he has taken the physical demands of it in his stride. Across the past six seasons, STATSports - a sports technology company Kane has invested in - found his distance covered, high-speed running and accelerations were up 8%, 22% and 42% respectively.

And given how the tactical landscape has changed over that time, it is particularly impressive Kane has been able to not only keep up, but stay ahead.

"Over the last five or six years, man-to-man pressure has become bigger," Kane says.

"European football is physical and top teams are trying to win the ball back high, trusting their defenders and midfielders to defend man for man to win their battles."

Given that change, the best teams have recruited physical athletes and brilliant dribblers who can beat their man when the game becomes a series of one-against-ones.

Kane, not known for his dribbling - and by his own admission "not the fastest", has thrived on his own terms.

Against Dortmund, there was a specific moment Kane dropped deep, looking to arrive in space unmarked. Recognising the danger, two players converged on the Englishman.

Kane's dribbling is cerebral. His speed of thought provides him solutions to problems others would attempt to solve with their feet alone.

After getting low and using his strength to shrug centre-back Waldemar Anton off him, Kane rose, slightly adjusting his body to the right. These micro-adjustments are a hallmark of his game and through them he is able to shift an entire team's momentum.

Fooled by this feint, Daniel Svensson and Jobe Bellingham found themselves wrong-footed as Kane snapped the ball back the other way, opening up the entire pitch from within Bayern's half.

Earlier this year, Bayern boss Vincent Kompany shed light on Kane's unique role, explaining it as being 50% coached and 50% Kane deciding what to do.

"I think it's partly instinct, using my football brain and getting the feeling on the pitch," says Kane. "If, for example, I want to drop and see if the centre-back really wants to commit, he might commit into midfield, but is he going to commit if I drop all the way to my box?

"After the first five or 10 minutes you really get an understanding of how the opposition are going to play, which dictates how I play."

There is a shared understanding at Bayern of an approach that allows team-mates to make sense of rotations that, to the naked eye, appear random.

Kane, who is given more freedom than most, is at the centre of it.

"I feel like my position now is as one of two 10s, and you work together," he says. "You can double up on one side to overload, which causes the opposition centre-backs a problem of who to mark.

"If they want to mark both, they've got to go man-to-man and then that leaves space for our wingers or full-backs to run into.

"It's posing all these questions to the opposition but, personally, I love having someone close to me who I can link with."

Kane built his reputation playing as a lone number nine, so it is interesting to hear him identify instead as a number 10 - in a front two.

"When you're the number nine on your own you can get marked by two centre-backs and you struggle to get touches on the ball," he says. "You're relying on everyone else to find you with the ball."

Showing Kane two clips from last season, I ask him to talk through what was going through his head.

"The thing with our formation is, as long as there's someone in each position, it doesn't really matter who it is. Lucho [Luis Diaz] in this clip is playing as one of those 10s.

"I've come off to try and create a bit of space and Lucho's gone through the centre."

Distracted by Kane's dropping-deep movement, one of the opposition midfielders is pulled towards him. This creates space, allowing Joshua Kimmich to punch the ball through to Diaz.

"I think it's Serge [Gnabry] making the run in behind which takes the defenders back, which allows me and Lucho that space in between. Lucho lays it off and whenever I'm in that position, around 20-25 yards out, I'm always looking if I can get my shot off."

It is one of many examples of Kane initially dropping deep before scoring.

"By playing deep when the play develops, I end up coming into a number 10 spot when everyone's dropped," he says. "I can get shots off from the edge of the box, which is a big strength of mine, or I'm running off the back of players where no-one's picking me up - because the midfielder finds it hard to [track]."

The second clip is from Bayern's Champions League tie against Club Brugge.

Usually Kane is marked by an opposition centre-back, but the Belgian club give that responsibility to their holding midfielder - something he recognises and exploits.

Lennart Karl scores without Kane touching the ball, but the striker's involvement is undeniable.

"These are the little runs, again, not everyone sees," Kane explains. "With Jamal Musiala and Lenny, they're so good at receiving the ball and dribbling so there'll be times where I will actually stay higher and let those guys get on the ball a bit deeper, and I'll try and make runs in behind.

"Without changing my game too much, I try and complement the players around me.

"I know Lenny is so good in those pockets and when he gets there, I'm more thinking of running in behind because, one, he can play me in and I can go through on goal, or two, he can dribble with the ball and do exactly what happened here.

"As soon as Lenny gets in that pocket I make the run and not always to get the ball, sometimes it is just to drag the defender away.

"Now he's one-against-one with a centre-back in the middle of the pitch and that's dangerous for any centre-back."

With the Ballon d'Or announcement on the horizon, Kane's name is in the conversation, primarily for the sheer volume of goals he has scored. What is easier to miss in that debate is the rest of his game.

Kane plays for the team in each phase of the game across the entirety of the pitch, while at the same time producing extraordinary individual numbers that match the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Erling Haaland.

He has described himself as playing in the role of a number 10, nine and six at times.

In a football world of specific and heavily drilled tactical roles, that is quite the achievement.

articles.title: El efecto dominó de Balogun: ni Everton, ni Conference... ¿por desconfianza?
articles.standfirst: Tras quedarse al final en Mónaco, Filipe Luis deja al estadounidense fuera de la lista de la fase liga de la tercera competición continental en importancia
articles.summary: Tras quedarse al final en Mónaco, Filipe Luis deja al estadounidense fuera de la lista de la fase liga de la tercera competición continental en importancia
articles.body: El Everton y el Mónaco no llegaron al final a un acuerdo por uno de los protagonistas del pasado Mundial: Foralin Balogun, delantero internacional con Estados Unidos. El club de Merseyside fue uno de tantos, como el Tottenham o incluso el PSG, que rondaron como candidatos al futbolista, que sin embargo no verá consumado su regreso a la Premier. No hay que olvidar que procede del filial gunner, que dejó por un traspaso de 40 millones de euros en 2023. Y no sólo eso. por más que en el Principado cosechó el curso pasado su mejor su mejor campaña como profesional (19 goles y 5 asistencias en 43 partidos la pasada temporada 2025-26), ha visto cómo su actual entrenador, el exrojiblanco Filipe Luis, no le ha incluido en la lista oficial del AS Monaco que disputará la fase liga de la Conference League. El mercado de fichajes es incierto. Lo que parece claro se puede torcer justo en el instante anterior de estampar una firma. Basta una mala sensación y alguna de las partes puede echarse atrás. Con Balogun pudo suceder algo parecido, al menos, eso es lo que expone en el CEO del AS Monaco, Thiago Scuro, quien según L'Equipe, fue el propio Falorin Balogun quien no quiso firmar. Como relata el diario galo, el Everton detectó un problema médico que requería una segunda opinión. Cinco minutos antes del cierre del mercado de fichajes, Scuro había firmado el contrato, y los Toffees también, pero al final fue el estadounidense el que no firmó al sentirse incómodo por la desconfianza mostrada por el Everton en las pruebas médicas. Pese a todo, y ante esta situación que ha provocado que en estos momentos el equipo monegasco tenga overbooking ofensivo, tampoco se descarta una salida a un equipo de ligas que aún tienen el mercado de fichajes operativo. A priori, el atacante no entrará en liza este viernes contra el Paris Saint Germain, se verá qué sucede al final con él. Si hay un episodio que ha marcado el año de Balogun, ese es sin duda su paso por el Mundial de 2026. El delantero fue una de las grandes revelaciones del combinado que dirige Mauricio Pochettino, y precisamente en el partido de dieciseisavos de final ante Bosnia y Herzegovina protagonizó una de las jugadas más comentadas del torneo: tras adelantar a Estados Unidos con un gol en la primera parte, Balogun vio la tarjeta roja directa en el minuto 64 por una entrada sobre el bosnio Tarik Muharemović, calificada como "juego brusco grave" tras revisión del VAR. Lo insólito llegó después: la FIFA, en una decisión sin precedentes que provocó un comunicado de protesta de la UEFA ("cruzó una línea roja", llegó a decir el organismo europeo), aplicó el artículo 27 de su código disciplinario para suspender la ejecución de la sanción, dejando a Balogun disponible para el partido de octavos ante Bélgica. La polémica escaló hasta la política, con el propio presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, reconociendo haber llamado personalmente al presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, para pedir la revisión del caso.
